The downsides of serving the model through a Kaggle notebook tunnel include:

- **Ephemeral:** The tunnel URL changes every time the notebook restarts, and Kaggle sessions are capped at approximately 12 hours and time out on idle. This makes it fine for a demo or recording session, but unsuitable for always-on hosting (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > !OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama pull qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M > Caveats (note for reflection log)).
- **Latency:** Each generation requires a round-trip from laptop to Cloudflare to the GPU. While still far faster than local CPU, it is not instant (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > !OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama pull qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M > Caveats (note for reflection log)).
- **Open endpoint:** A `trycloudflare.com` URL is public while it is up. Although the risk is low (just an LLM, no persistent data storage), you should not leave it running unattended or send sensitive input (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > !OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama pull qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M > Caveats (note for reflection log)).
- **Reproducibility:** You need to explicitly record which model and platform produced any results you keep for a dissertation or report (noting both the `OLLAMA_MODEL` value and the platform, e.g., "Kaggle T4") (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > !OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama pull qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M > Caveats (note for reflection log)).

The consent-gate classifier labels player utterances into four event types, each affecting the trust score as follows:

| Event | Trust Change ($\Delta$) | Description / Example |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `deescalation_lever` | **+15** | Empathetic or calming player input (e.g., *"Ray, I can see this is frightening — take your time."*) |
| `plain_explanation` | **+10** | Clear, patient-focused explanations (e.g., *"The heart tracing tells me if your heart's short of blood — that's why it matters to you."*) |
| `neutral` | **0** | Standard procedural or informational questions (e.g., *"How long have you had the pain?"*) |
| `escalation_trigger` | **−20** | Confrontational, dismissive, or pressuring input (e.g., *"You need to calm down and let me do my job."*) |

(docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine > Event taxonomy (what the classifier must label each player utterance as))

Based on the documentation, the following parts of the consent gate have not been validated yet:

* **The agents/LLM side of the loop** (Ollama wasn't brought up alongside the Convex backend, so only the map/schema/data layer was validated) (docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine).
* **An actual in-browser click-through of the test menu** to confirm that a refused push shows Ray's refusal line, a permitted push posts the result message into the chat, and the trust-state prompt line measurably changes the local model's patient-agent dialogue (docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine).
* **An end-to-end in-world run with a human clinician**, which needs the UI panel and a running engine (docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine > Not validated yet (honest scope)).
* **The classifier's accuracy** at labelling free-text utterances (using a keyword baseline first) (docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine > Not validated yet (honest scope)).
* **Latency and quality of the patient agent's *spoken* refusals**, which waits on GPU compute (docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine > Not validated yet (honest scope)).

Scenario difficulty is tuned by mapping the persona card's "Difficulty dial" (which covers hostility, bystander panic, and time pressure) onto `START_TRUST` and the gain/loss magnitudes, while all thresholds and deltas are configured as constants at the top of `consentGate.ts` (`START_TRUST`, `DEESCALATION_GAIN`, `WARY_AT`, `CONSENTING_AT`, `SELF_DISCHARGE_REFUSALS`, etc.) (docs/consent_gate.md > VeriSim Consent-Gate — Design Spec & State Machine > Tuning / difficulty dial).

To run Ares, you need the following installed:

- Python 3.12+ (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Requirements)
- Ollama with the models in `ares/config.py` pulled (`start.sh` tells you which are missing) (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Requirements)
- Docker, for the optional Langfuse tracing stack (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Requirements)
- Serena on your `PATH`, for `/serena` (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Requirements)
To point Ares's `/serena` command at a different codebase, set the `ARES_SERENA_PROJECT` environment variable (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Run).
